rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes partial Ta-to-Ti substitution, whereas the paper compared a full equiatomic substitution (CrFeTaVW vs CrFeTiVW). The hypothesis also frames the intervention as a controlled fraction replacement, while the paper studied a complete compositional swap.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies 400–800°C and cyclic mechanical loading, while the paper used simulations from 300–2100 K, SPS consolidation at ~1543 K, and thermal diffusivity measurements from 300–1000 K under He, with no cyclic mechanical loading.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes enhanced phonon-mediated heat transfer and microstructural refinement for mechanical integrity. The paper found that Ta/Ti substitution did not materially change thermal diffusivity, attributed transport to multielement disorder and lattice expansion, and observed phase changes (Laves phase vs two bcc phases) rather than a mechanism that enhances heat transfer.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts higher thermal conductivity with similar or improved mechanical performance. The paper found similar thermal diffusivity for both alloys and did not measure mechanical properties; the predicted outcome direction (improvement) contradicts the paper's finding of no material change in thermal transport.
